{{Short description|German physicist and meteorologist}}

'''Volker Wulfmeyer''' (born 8 October 1965)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Volker Wulfmeyer |url=https://www.degruyter.com/database/KDGO/entry/P108456/html?lang=de |access-date=2023-07-19 |website=De Gruyter |language=de}}</ref> is a German physicist, [[meteorologist]], [[climate]] and [[Earth system science|earth system]] researcher, university professor, and member of the [[Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities|Heidelberg Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hohenheim |first=Universität |title=Prof. Dr. Volker Wulfmeyer: Institut für Physik und Meteorologie |url=https://physik-meteorologie.uni-hohenheim.de/volker-wulfmeyer |access-date=2023-07-19 |website=physik-meteorologie.uni-hohenheim.de |language=de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Unsere Mitglieder {{!}} Heidelberger Akademie der Wissenschaften |url=https://www.hadw-bw.de/mitglieder?n=W&a=1 |access-date=2023-07-19 |website=www.hadw-bw.de}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Wulfmeyer received his doctorate in 1995 from the [[University of Hamburg]] and [[Max Planck Institute for Meteorology|Max-Planck-Institute for Meteorology]] under [[Hartmut Graßl]] and Jens Bösenberg in the Department of Geosciences with the thesis "[[Lidar|DIAL]] Measurements of Vertical Water Vapor Distributions".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wulfmeyer |first=Volker |date=2023-07-19 |title=DIAL-MESSUNGEN VON VERTIKALEN WASSERDAMPFVERTEILUNGEN |url=https://pure.mpg.de/rest/items/item_3195172/component/file_3195173/content |access-date=2023-07-19 |website=www.pure.mpg.de}}</ref> Under a [[Feodor Lynen]] Fellowship from the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]], he worked as a [[postdoctoral researcher]] and leader of the joint [[National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration|NOAA]]-[[National Center for Atmospheric Research|NCAR]] lidar research team in [[Boulder, Colorado|Boulder]] ([[Colorado]]), US, from 1996 to 1998, and as a scientist at NCAR from 1998 to 2000.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Profil |url=https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/vernetzen/recherche-im-humboldt-netzwerk/einzelansicht?tx_rsmavhsolr_solrviewhumboldtians%5BpPersonId%5D=1051308&cHash=b6c63f134195b9858cb21bc9c9a425d8 |access-date=2023-07-19 |website=www.humboldt-foundation.de |language=en}}</ref>

Since February 2001, Wulfmeyer is a university professor, the managing director of the Institute of Physics and Meteorology and holder of the Chair of Physics and Meteorology at the [[University of Hohenheim]] in [[Stuttgart]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hohenheim |first=Universität |title=Prof. Dr. Volker Wulfmeyer: Institut für Physik und Meteorologie |url=https://physik-meteorologie.uni-hohenheim.de/volker-wulfmeyer |access-date=2023-07-19 |website=physik-meteorologie.uni-hohenheim.de |language=de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hohenheim |first=Universität |title=PM Detailansicht: Universität Hohenheim |url=https://www.uni-hohenheim.de/pressemitteilung?tx_ttnews%5Btt_news%5D=43963&cHash=df4b1a9aacb39e5fe7d07e82ae8ca12f |access-date=2023-07-19 |website=www.uni-hohenheim.de |language=de}}</ref>

== Research and projects ==
Based on his work at NOAA and NCAR, Wulfmeyer developed suitable sensor synergies to study turbulent transport processes in the convective [[boundary layer]], mesoscale circulations in complex terrain, exchange processes at the land surface, entrainment processes at the top of the boundary layer, and generally to study land-atmosphere feedback.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Wulfmeyer In parallel, his team at the University of Hohenheim further optimized the [[Weather Research and Forecasting Model|WRF]]-NOAHMP land-atmosphere model, which has been used for a wide variety of model studies, including turbulence analyses, air pollution over Stuttgart, [[bio-geoengineering]] approaches, high-resolution weather forecasts, impact studies for [[data assimilation]], and regional climate simulations.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Warrach-Sagi |first1=Kirsten |last2=Schwitalla |first2=Thomas |last3=Wulfmeyer |first3=Volker |last4=Bauer |first4=Hans-Stefan |date=2013-08-01 In recent years, [[machine learning]] approaches have also found their way into this research portfolio, e.g., to study exchange processes at the land surface.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Wulfmeyer |first1=Volker |last2=Pineda |first2=Juan Manuel Valencia |last3=Otte |first3=Sebastian |last4=Karlbauer |first4=Matthias |last5=Butz |first5=Martin V. |last6=Lee |first6=Temple R. |last7=Rajtschan |first7=Verena |date=2023-02-01 |title=Estimation of the Surface Fluxes for Heat and Momentum in Unstable Conditions with Machine Learning and Similarity Approaches for the LAFE Data Set |journal=Boundary-Layer Meteorology |language=en |volume=186 |issue=2 |pages=337–371 |doi=10.1007/s10546-022-00761-2 |bibcode=2023BoLMe.186..337W |s2cid=253863297 |issn=1573-1472|doi-access=free }}</ref> Currently, his team is expanding the Land Atmosphere Feedback Observatory (LAFO), which is used to study the land-atmosphere system.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hohenheim |first=Universität |title=Daten: Land-Atmosphäre Feedback Observatorium (LAFO) |url=https://lafo.uni-hohenheim.de/daten |access-date=2023-07-19 |website=lafo.uni-hohenheim.de |language=de}}</ref>

Since 2020 Wulfmeyer is a member of the WCRP panel Global Land/Atmosphere System Study (GLASS) of the Global Energy and Water Exchanges ([[GEWEX]]).<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-03-16 |title=GLASS Panel Members {{!}} GEWEX |url=https://www.gewex.org/panels/global-landatmosphere-system-study-panel/glass-panel/ |access-date=2023-07-19 |website=GEWEX {{!}} The Global Energy and Water Exchanges (GEWEX) program, a core project of the World Climate Research Programme (WCRP), is dedicated to understanding Earth's water cycle and energy fluxes at and below the surface and in the atmosphere. We are a network of scientists gathering information on the global water and energy cycles through research, observations, and science activities, which will help to predict changes in the world's climate |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Volker Wulfmeyer zum Mitglied des GLASS-Panels ernannt {{!}} Heidelberger Akademie der Wissenschaften |url=https://www.hadw-bw.de/news/volker-wulfmeyer-zum-mitglied-des-glass-panels-ernannt |access-date=2023-07-19 |website=www.hadw-bw.de}}</ref>

== Other interests and activities ==
Being a co-signer of the declaration "[[Scientists for Future]]" and co-founder of the regional group of this movement in Stuttgart, Wulfmeyer also deals with problems and issues raised by [[climate change]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ackermann |first=Eduard |date=2023-07-19 |title=Zur Person von Professor Wulfmeyer |url=http://www.katholische-kirche-eningen.de/fileadmin/user_upload/userdata/Gruppen/Oekumene/oekumene_2020/2003_Wulfmeyer.pdf |access-date=2023-07-19 |website=www.katholische-kirche-eningen.de |archive-date=2023-03-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230327193925/http://www.katholische-kirche-eningen.de/fileadmin/user_upload/userdata/Gruppen/Oekumene/oekumene_2020/2003_Wulfmeyer.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hohenheim |first=Universität |title=PM Detailansicht: Universität Hohenheim |url=https://www.uni-hohenheim.de/pressemitteilung?tx_ttnews%5Btt_news%5D=43963&cHash=df4b1a9aacb39e5fe7d07e82ae8ca12f |access-date=2023-07-19 |website=www.uni-hohenheim.de |language=de}}</ref> As part of this commitment, Wulfmeyer initiated the founding of the Climate Crisis Working Group at the [[Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities]], which held a series of lectures on the subject and published a special issue.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Academy for Future {{!}} Heidelberger Akademie der Wissenschaften |url=https://hadw-bw.de/academy-future |access-date=2023-07-19 |website=hadw-bw.de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Akademie der Wissenschaften des Landes Baden-Württemberg |first=Heidelberger Akademie der Wissenschaften |date=2023-07-19 |title=KLIMAKRISE.GEISTES- & NATURWISSENSCHAFTLICHE HERAUSFORDERUNGEN UND ZUSAMMENHÄNGE |url=https://hadw-bw.de/sites/default/files/documents/Athene_2-2022.pdf |access-date=2023-07-19 |website=www.hadw-bw.de}}</ref>
